what_this_is: The two-grader grounding pack for docs/06 §7.4 item 1. Twenty spoken, cited claims from a fresh run of Harness A and Harness B, each with the full text of every chunk it cites, ready for two independent human graders. Nothing here is graded: §7.4 requires human labels before an LLM judge ships, and the published semantic rate (70% post-4.4) has one grader and no κ, which is why this pack exists. The previous grader's verdicts are deliberately NOT in this pack.

how_the_sample_was_drawn.replacement_rule: in order from eval.grounding.sample_claims(pool, size=20, seed=45), skipping claims already carried
how_the_sample_was_drawn.caveat: Claims carried forward keep the denominator comparable with the pre-4.4 and post-4.4 gradings. They also mean this is not an independent redraw of the population — read the rate as a property of these claims, not of the agent.

rubric: supported — the cited chunk states the fact the line asserts, or documents the condition/procedure the line asks about.
partial — the chunk is on the same topic but does not contain the specific thing asserted or asked. Scores 0: the measurement is whether the chunk supports the claim AS STATED.
unsupported — the chunk does not bear on the line at all. Scores 0.
Where a line cites several chunks, one supporting chunk is enough; the note says which one carried it.

A question that offers an option the corpus does not name (a battery pack, an OS version) is still supported if the chunk carries the distinction the question turns on. The option is offered, not asserted.
grading_is_a_human_step: Two independent human graders fill sheet.csv (one copy each), then eval/score_grading.py prints Cohen's κ and the rates. No model grades these claims.

My Camera does NOT Turn ON

ROVE Dash Cam Troubleshooting

My camera does not turn on — here's how to fix it.

Follow these step-by-step options to identify what's preventing your ROVE dash cam from powering on and get back on the road quickly.

Start troubleshooting Contact support

Check the power source

A faulty cable or charger is the most common reason a dash cam won't power on.

Try without memory card

A corrupted or incompatible memory card can sometimes prevent the camera from booting.

Reset the camera

A quick reset with a paper clip can resolve a frozen or unresponsive dash cam.

Before you begin

Bring the camera indoors and use your iPhone or Android smartphone's USB charger along with the short USB cable included in the ROVE box. Plug everything into a standard 110V wall outlet — not your car — to eliminate vehicle power as a variable.

Work through each option below in order. This process helps pinpoint whether the issue is the cable, the charger, or the camera itself.

Step-by-step troubleshooting

Try these options one by one

Option 1

Test with a different USB cable

Swap to the 12FT long L-shaped power cable or the short 1M USB cable — both are included in your ROVE box. Connect it to your smartphone's USB charger and plug it into a wall outlet.

✅ What to look for: If the camera powers on with a different cable, the original cable is defective and needs to be replaced.

Option 2

Remove the memory card

Eject the microSD card from the camera. Unplug the power cable, then plug it back in. Check if the camera powers on without the memory card inserted.

✅ What to look for: If the camera turns on without the card, the memory card may be corrupted or incompatible. Try a new card.

Option 3

Press the Power button once

With the power cable plugged in, press the Power button once. On some ROVE models, the camera does not automatically power on when connected — a single press of the power button is required.

✅ What to look for: The screen should light up within a few seconds of pressing the button.

Option 4

Perform a hard reset

Locate the Reset button at the bottom of the dash cam. Use a straightened paper clip or a pen tip to press and hold the reset button once while the power cord is plugged in.

If the camera still does not turn on, unplug the power cable first, then repeat the reset process.

⚠️ Where to find it: The Reset button is located at the bottom of the camera, near the Serial Number label (R2XXXXXXXXX).

Quick troubleshooting order

Swap cable → Remove memory card → Press Power button → Perform hard reset → Contact ROVE support

Diagnosis Guide

What each test tells you

Camera turns on with a different cable The original USB cable is defective. Contact ROVE support to request a replacement cable under warranty.

Camera turns on without the memory card The microSD card may be corrupted, full, or incompatible. Try formatting the card or replacing it with a new one (Class 10 / U3 recommended).

Camera does not turn on after all options The camera unit itself may be defective. Please reach out to ROVE support — we'll promptly replace any defective item under the warranty to ensure your complete satisfaction.

Still need help? No worries.

At ROVE, your satisfaction means the world to us. Our customer care team is here 7 days a week and will promptly replace any defective item to ensure your complete satisfaction.

cited_chunks.section: Why is my video blurry or out of focus?
cited_chunks.text:
Why is my video blurry or out of focus?

ROVE Dash Cam Video Quality Guide

Why is my video blurry or out of focus?

If your dash cam video looks blurry, foggy, hazy, or out of focus, the cause is usually something simple: a protective film, a dirty lens, windshield haze, low-light conditions, or a lower video resolution setting.

✅ Start with the lens and windshield first — they are the most common causes of blurry footage.

Remove lens film

New dash cams may have a clear protective film over the lens that must be removed.

Clean glass and lens

Fingerprints, dust, windshield fog, and interior haze can make footage look soft or cloudy.

Check resolution

Lower recording resolutions will look less detailed than 4K or 2.5K settings.

Before you begin

Blurry video is usually caused by something in front of the lens

The dash cam can only record clearly if the lens and windshield are clear. Protective film, fingerprints, dust, fog, windshield residue, glare, or condensation can all make the video appear blurry even when the camera is working normally.

Follow the steps below in order. After each step, record a short test video in daylight and review the original video file.

Step-by-step fix

How to improve blurry or out-of-focus video

Step 1

Check this first

Remove the protective lens film

Many new dash cams have a clear protective plastic film over the lens. If this film is still attached, videos may look blurry, foggy, or out of focus.

✅ Tip: Check both the front camera lens and rear camera lens if your model includes a rear camera.

Step 2

Clean lens

Clean the dash cam lens

Fingerprints, dust, residue, or smudges can affect video clarity. Gently wipe the lens using a soft, clean microfiber cloth.

⚠️ Important: Do not use harsh chemicals or rough materials on the lens. A soft microfiber cloth is best.

Step 3

Check windshield

Clean the windshield inside and outside

Fog, condensation, dust, dirt, or oily film on the windshield can make the video look hazy or soft. Clean the glass inside and outside, especially the area directly in front of the camera lens.

✅ Best result: Test the camera again in daylight after cleaning the windshield and lens.

Step 4

Low light

Understand low-light video limits

Night driving, very dark scenes, rain, glare, or strong headlights may make the video appear grainy or less sharp. This can be normal in low-light conditions.

What may help:

• Test again during daylight

• Check if HDR is available and enabled on your model

• Avoid placing the camera behind heavy tint or dirty glass

• Adjust exposure if your model supports it

Step 5

Resolution setting

Check the video resolution setting

If the camera is set to a lower resolution, the video will look less detailed. Go to the video settings and select a higher resolution, such as 4K or 2.5K, if your model supports it.

✅ Tip: For the clearest review, transfer the original video file to a computer and play it using a compatible video player.

Quick Summary

What usually fixes blurry or foggy video?

🎞️ Remove protective film Make sure the clear plastic film has been removed from the lens.

🧼 Clean the lens and windshield Smudges, dust, fog, and windshield haze are the most common causes of blurry footage.

🎥 Check resolution and lighting Low resolution or low-light conditions can make footage appear less sharp.

Still need help? We're here.

cited_chunks.section: Why Is My Dashcam Overheating — What Causes It and How Can I Prevent It?
cited_chunks.text:
Why Is My Dashcam Overheating — What Causes It and How Can I Prevent It?

It’s normal for your ROVE dash cam to feel warm during regular use, especially when recording in 4K, operating in Parking Mode, or running under direct sunlight.

However, if your device becomes unusually hot, shuts down unexpectedly, or displays a high-temperature warning, it may be overheating—and that’s something we want to help you avoid.

1. Extended Exposure to Direct Sunlight

When your vehicle is parked under the sun, especially during summer, cabin temperatures can exceed 140°F (60°C). Prolonged exposure can cause your dash cam’s internal temperature to rise above its normal operating range.

ROVE dash cams are designed to operate between -4°F and 140°F (-20°C to 60°C). To protect itself, the device may slow down, shut off, or stop recording beyond that.

2. Incompatible or Faulty MicroSD Card

A low-quality or non-U3-rated memory card can force the camera’s processor to work harder when saving video files, generating additional heat. Some cards may also fail to write correctly, causing the camera to freeze or overheat.

3. Using Unsupported Power Sources

Power banks, OBD2 adapters, and third-party USB chargers may not supply consistent voltage or include built-in protections. This can cause the dash cam to draw unstable current, increasing heat buildup over time.

4. Parking Mode Running in Extreme Heat

When Parking Mode is active, the dash cam remains on standby or records at a low bitrate while the vehicle is off. Without air circulation or A/C, interior temperatures can spike quickly, increasing the risk of overheating—especially if Parking Mode is left running for long periods.

Here are some practical steps to keep your dash cam running safely and efficiently:
1. Use a High-Quality, U3-Class MicroSD Card

We recommend using a ROVE PRO, ROVE Ultimate, or ROVE Industrial U3 microSD card. These are designed for high-speed 4K recording and maintain stable write speeds, reducing stress on the camera’s processor.

2. Format the Memory Card Regularly

To prevent file system errors and minimize write stress, format your SD card in-camera once every 1-2 weeks.

3. Avoid Direct Sunlight

Whenever possible, park in the shade or use a windshield sunshade to keep the cabin temperature lower. If your vehicle allows, mount the dash cam away from direct sunlight.

4. Use Only ROVE-Approved Power Sources

Use the original ROVE USB-C car charger or the ROVE Ultimate 3-Lead Hardwire Kit for stable and safe operation. These provide a regulated 5V/3.4A output and include built-in protection for your dash cam and your vehicle’s battery.

5. Adjust Parking Mode Settings

If you're in a high-heat region, consider setting a shorter Parking Mode timer (1-3 hours) or disabling it during hotter days. This helps prevent your camera from running too long while the cabin temperature rises.

6. Keep Firmware Up to Date

We release firmware updates to improve performance, fix bugs, and optimize heat management. If you’re unsure of your current version, contact our support team, and we’ll provide the latest version and installation instructions.

Is This Covered Under Warranty?

If your dash cam consistently overheats, shuts off without warning, or displays a “High Temperature” error, it could be a sign of a hardware issue. Please stop using the device and contact us right away. If it’s still under warranty, we’ll work with you on repair or replacement options.

cited_chunks.text:
Join the “ROVE_R***_*******” network using the default password “12345678” displayed on your dash camera’s screen

For an Android user, there is one extra step you will have to take for the first time. Once you connect to Dash Cam’s WiFi, it will say “No Internet”. Which is fine. Wait about 10-15 seconds until you see the below pop-up or notification. You just have to tap on the pop-up notification that will show up in a few seconds to select that you still want to stay connected even though there is NO Internet. Once you select this OK, you are set to go.

Once your smartphone is connected to the ROVE Dash Cam WiFi, go back to the ROVE APP and you should see the live video feed from the camera on the main home screen of the ROVE APP. Now you are all set to access your recording from the ROVE app and explore it further.

We hope this guide has been helpful in understanding how the WiFi feature works for ROVE Dash Cameras. Please feel free to reach out to us if you have any questions or concerns.

If You Still Unable To Connect The Wifi, Please Follow These Additional Step Below:

Check Dash Cam Power and Memory Card: Ensure that your dash cam is powered on, and a compatible memory card is properly inserted. Sometimes, connectivity issues can arise if the dash cam is not powered on or if the memory card is not inserted correctly.

Signal Interference: WiFi signals can be affected by interference from other electronic devices or physical obstructions. Make sure the phone is within the 10M Range from the dash cam and there is not obstructions between the camera and your phone. Additionally, try moving closer to the dash cam to strengthen the WiFi signal.

Firmware Update: Check if there are any available firmware updates for your dash cam. Updating the firmware can often resolve connectivity issues and improve overall performance. You can usually find firmware update files on the ROVE’s website or when the Wi-Fi is connected you can remotely update your firmware over the air using the ROVE App.

Reset Network Settings: If you continue to experience WiFi connectivity issues, you can try resetting the network settings on your mobile device. This will reset all network-related settings to default configurations, potentially resolving any underlying network configuration issues.

If none of the above steps resolve the WiFi connectivity problem, please don't hesitate to contact our customer support team for further assistance. Our dedicated support team is available to help troubleshoot any issues you may encounter and provide personalized assistance to ensure your ROVE dash cam operates smoothly.

cited_chunks.text:
Why can’t I read the license plate number clearly?

ROVE Dash Cam Video Quality Guide

Why can’t I read the license plate number clearly?

License plate clarity depends on lighting, distance, speed, angle, windshield glare, video resolution, and how the video is played back. This guide explains what affects plate readability and how to get the best possible footage from your ROVE dash cam.

✅ For best results, review original video files using VLC Media Player or the ROVE GPS Player.

Lighting matters

Bright glare, darkness, headlights, shadows, and reflections can affect plate readability.

Distance & speed matter

The farther or faster the vehicle is, the harder it is for any dash cam to capture clear plate details.

Use the right player

Windows Media Player may play high-bitrate 4K videos poorly. VLC or ROVE GPS Player is recommended.

Why this happens

License plate capture is affected by real-world driving conditions

Your ROVE dash cam records high-quality video, but reading license plates depends on multiple factors, including proper lighting, focal distance, how close the vehicle is, driving speed, camera angle, glare, reflections, and video playback quality.

For example, a plate may be easy to read when the vehicle is close, centered, and well-lit, but difficult to read if the vehicle is far away, moving quickly, at an angle, or affected by headlights or windshield glare.

Step-by-step improvement guide

How to improve license plate readability

Step 1

Driving conditions

Understand real-world capture limits

License plates are easier to read when the vehicle is close, centered, and moving at a similar speed. Plates may be harder to read when the vehicle is far away, at a sharp angle, moving quickly, or affected by glare, headlights, shadows, rain, or dirty glass.

✅ Best chance for plate capture: Good lighting, close distance, straight angle, clean windshield, and stable playback from the original file.

Step 2

Improve clarity

Clean the windshield and lens

A dirty windshield, a fingerprint on the lens, glare, or reflection can reduce clarity. Clean the windshield area in front of the lens and gently clean the dash cam lens with a soft microfiber cloth.

Step 3

Check playback first

Play the original file using VLC Media Player

Do not judge video quality from a compressed copy, social media upload, text message, or phone preview. Transfer the original video file to your computer and play it using VLC Media Player.

⚠️ Important: Windows Media Player is not recommended for high-bitrate 4K dash cam videos because playback may appear choppy or unclear.

Step 4

Use ROVE GPS Player

Try the ROVE GPS Player

You can also use the ROVE GPS Player from our website to view your videos with Google Maps, G-sensor data, date, direction, and speed during playback.

If your ROVE dash cam displays a “Memory Card Too Slow” message, it usually means the memory card can no longer maintain the required write speed for continuous video recording.

Memory cards have a limited lifespan. Over time, repeated recording and overwriting may cause the card to slow down, develop bad sectors, or become corrupted.

In most cases, this warning means your dash cam is functioning properly and is simply alerting you that the memory card may need maintenance or replacement.

Before you begin

A “Memory Card Too Slow” message usually means the memory card can no longer maintain the required write speed for continuous recording.

Format the Memory Card

Replace the Memory Card

Replace the memory card with a Class 10 U3 high-speed microSD card recommended for dash cam use.

Upgrade to a High-Speed ROVE Memory Card

For an Android user, there is one extra step you will have to take for the first time. Once you connect to Dash Cam’s WiFi, it will say “No Internet”. Which is fine. Wait about 10-15 seconds until you see the below pop-up or notification. You just have to tap on the pop-up notification that will show up in a few seconds to select that you still want to stay connected even though there is NO Internet. If You Still Unable To Connect The Wifi, Please Follow These Additional Step Below:

Check Dash Cam Power and Memory Card: Ensure that your dash cam is powered on, and a compatible memory card is properly inserted. Sometimes, connectivity issues can arise if the dash cam is not powered on or if the memory card is not inserted correctly.

Signal Interference: WiFi signals can be affected by interference from other electronic devices or physical obstructions. Make sure the phone is within the 10M Range from the dash cam and there is not obstructions between the camera and your phone. Additionally, try moving closer to the dash cam to strengthen the WiFi signal.

Firmware Update: Check if there are any available firmware updates for your dash cam. Updating the firmware can often resolve connectivity issues and improve overall performance. You can usually find firmware update files on the ROVE’s website or when the Wi-Fi is connected you can remotely update your firmware over the air using the ROVE App.

Reset Network Settings: If you continue to experience WiFi connectivity issues, you can try resetting the network settings on your mobile device. This will reset all network-related settings to default configurations, potentially resolving any underlying network configuration issues.

If none of the above steps resolve the WiFi connectivity problem, please don't hesitate to contact our customer support team for further assistance. cited_chunks.section: Why Is My Dashcam Overheating — What Causes It and How Can I Prevent It?
cited_chunks.text:
Why Is My Dashcam Overheating — What Causes It and How Can I Prevent It?

It’s normal for your ROVE dash cam to feel warm during regular use, especially when recording in 4K, operating in Parking Mode, or running under direct sunlight.

However, if your device becomes unusually hot, shuts down unexpectedly, or displays a high-temperature warning, it may be overheating—and that’s something we want to help you avoid.

1. Extended Exposure to Direct Sunlight

When your vehicle is parked under the sun, especially during summer, cabin temperatures can exceed 140°F (60°C). Prolonged exposure can cause your dash cam’s internal temperature to rise above its normal operating range.

ROVE dash cams are designed to operate between -4°F and 140°F (-20°C to 60°C). To protect itself, the device may slow down, shut off, or stop recording beyond that.

2. Incompatible or Faulty MicroSD Card

A low-quality or non-U3-rated memory card can force the camera’s processor to work harder when saving video files, generating additional heat. Some cards may also fail to write correctly, causing the camera to freeze or overheat.

3. Using Unsupported Power Sources

Power banks, OBD2 adapters, and third-party USB chargers may not supply consistent voltage or include built-in protections. This can cause the dash cam to draw unstable current, increasing heat buildup over time.

4. Parking Mode Running in Extreme Heat

When Parking Mode is active, the dash cam remains on standby or records at a low bitrate while the vehicle is off. Without air circulation or A/C, interior temperatures can spike quickly, increasing the risk of overheating—especially if Parking Mode is left running for long periods.

Here are some practical steps to keep your dash cam running safely and efficiently:
1. Use a High-Quality, U3-Class MicroSD Card

We recommend using a ROVE PRO, ROVE Ultimate, or ROVE Industrial U3 microSD card. These are designed for high-speed 4K recording and maintain stable write speeds, reducing stress on the camera’s processor.

2. Format the Memory Card Regularly

To prevent file system errors and minimize write stress, format your SD card in-camera once every 1-2 weeks.

3. Avoid Direct Sunlight

Whenever possible, park in the shade or use a windshield sunshade to keep the cabin temperature lower. If your vehicle allows, mount the dash cam away from direct sunlight.

4. Use Only ROVE-Approved Power Sources

Use the original ROVE USB-C car charger or the ROVE Ultimate 3-Lead Hardwire Kit for stable and safe operation. These provide a regulated 5V/3.4A output and include built-in protection for your dash cam and your vehicle’s battery.

5. Adjust Parking Mode Settings

If you're in a high-heat region, consider setting a shorter Parking Mode timer (1-3 hours) or disabling it during hotter days. This helps prevent your camera from running too long while the cabin temperature rises.

6. Keep Firmware Up to Date

We release firmware updates to improve performance, fix bugs, and optimize heat management. If you’re unsure of your current version, contact our support team, and we’ll provide the latest version and installation instructions.

Is This Covered Under Warranty?

If your dash cam consistently overheats, shuts off without warning, or displays a “High Temperature” error, it could be a sign of a hardware issue. Please stop using the device and contact us right away. If it’s still under warranty, we’ll work with you on repair or replacement options.

If You Still Unable To Connect The Wifi, Please Follow These Additional Step Below:

Check Dash Cam Power and Memory Card: Ensure that your dash cam is powered on, and a compatible memory card is properly inserted. Sometimes, connectivity issues can arise if the dash cam is not powered on or if the memory card is not inserted correctly.

Signal Interference: WiFi signals can be affected by interference from other electronic devices or physical obstructions. Make sure the phone is within the 10M Range from the dash cam and there is not obstructions between the camera and your phone. Additionally, try moving closer to the dash cam to strengthen the WiFi signal.

Firmware Update: Check if there are any available firmware updates for your dash cam. Updating the firmware can often resolve connectivity issues and improve overall performance. You can usually find firmware update files on the ROVE’s website or when the Wi-Fi is connected you can remotely update your firmware over the air using the ROVE App.

Reset Network Settings: If you continue to experience WiFi connectivity issues, you can try resetting the network settings on your mobile device. This will reset all network-related settings to default configurations, potentially resolving any underlying network configuration issues.

If none of the above steps resolve the WiFi connectivity problem, please don't hesitate to contact our customer support team for further assistance. Our dedicated support team is available to help troubleshoot any issues you may encounter and provide personalized assistance to ensure your ROVE dash cam operates smoothly.
